details: Bitcoin has fallen below the $60,000 mark, driven by significant net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs). BlackRock's IBIT alone recorded substantial redemptions, contributing to a cautious market sentiment exacerbated by macroeconomic concerns and a strengthening U.S. dollar.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $60K Amid Persistent ETF Outflows

details: Strategy (MSTR) has introduced a "BTC Monetization Program," allowing the company to sell up to $1.25 billion worth of Bitcoin. These sales are intended to fund its U.S. dollar reserves, cover preferred dividends and interest payments, and finance newly authorized share buybacks, marking a notable shift from its long-standing "HODL" strategy.
title: Strategy Authorizes Bitcoin Sales and Share Buybacks

details: Ethereum's price continues to trade below $1,600 amidst a broader market correction and ongoing ETF outflows. Despite the current bearish price action and sentiment, institutional entities like Bitmine Immersion Technologies and SharpLink Gaming have increased their ETH holdings, indicating long-term conviction among some large investors.
title: Ethereum Struggles Below $1,600 as Whales Accumulate

details: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has published its final comprehensive crypto regulatory framework. Key elements include mandatory licensing for crypto firms, capital requirements, and market abuse rules, with the full authorization regime set to commence on October 25, 2027.
title: UK Finalizes Crypto Regulatory Framework with 2027 Deadline

details: Over 140 firms, including Visa, Mastercard, and Coinbase, are launching "Open USD," a new stablecoin designed for efficient cross-border payments with no mint or redeem fees. Simultaneously, BNY Mellon has expanded its partnership with Circle, making USDC the first stablecoin directly supported on its Digital Asset Custody platform for institutional clients, enabling minting, redeeming, and transferring.
title: New Open USD Stablecoin & BNY Mellon Supports USDC
